metadata.title: hardening: auth/scope consistency, transport checks, and jmeter stability (p-h)
metadata.author: crivetimihai

description:
## Summary
This PR bundles a set of defensive hardening changes across auth/scoping, Streamable HTTP transport behavior, and load-test defaults.

These changes are framed as consistency and resilience hardening, not as newly disclosed security vulnerabilities.

## What Changed
- Hardened Streamable HTTP permission and session-ownership paths.
  - Added stricter RBAC/session access checks and deny-path test coverage.
  - Added explicit docstring/exception coverage where enforcement behavior changed.
- Removed a transport import cycle.
  - Replaced lazy import of `mcpgateway.main` from Streamable HTTP transport with explicit session-registry injection.
- Hardened permission enforcement semantics.
  - Public-only tokens (`teams=[]`) are explicitly blocked from satisfying `admin.*` permissions.
- Aligned NGINX gateway configs for safer auth/cache behavior consistency.
- Stabilized `make jmeter-load` defaults.
  - Updated default JMeter token generation to explicit admin-bypass claims when intended.
  - Removed `/reverse-proxy/sessions` from default REST mix (404 by default when reverse-proxy routes are disabled).
- Clarified docs for token-scoping semantics.
  - Added detailed `is_admin`/`teams`/`token_use` model and fixed inconsistent matrix examples.

## Why
- Reduce ambiguity between identity (`is_admin`) and visibility scope (`teams`).
- Keep enforcement behavior consistent across REST/RPC/Streamable HTTP and middleware/service layers.
- Remove expected-failure noise from default load testing so signal reflects real regressions.

## Scope
- Auth/scoping hardening
- Streamable HTTP transport hardening
- NGINX config consistency hardening
- JMeter profile reliability hardening
- RBAC/scoping documentation corrections
